name: Panorama Racławicka
blurb: Giant 1794 battle painting wrapped around a rotunda, showing the Battle of Racławice from every side. Wrocław's most-visited attraction.
priceText: 50 zł adults, 23 zł students & families (per person)
when: Apr–Sep daily 09:00–17:00; Oct–Mar Tue–Sun 09:00–16:00, Mon closed

name: Cathedral of St John the Baptist (tower)
blurb: Gothic cathedral with Poland's largest church organ; a lift takes you up the tower for river views over the city.
priceText: Tower 25 zł, reduced 20 zł for under-25s (official site); another official list shows 32 zł / 27 zł

name: Market Square (Rynek)
blurb: One of Europe's biggest town squares, ringed by photogenic old buildings and the centre of the city's social life.

name: Cathedral Island (Ostrów Tumski)
blurb: Islands on the Oder with brick cathedrals and narrow old streets; a free, atmospheric spot for an evening stroll.

name: Bar Pierożek, ul. Sądowa 7
blurb: Locals rate it Wrocław's best pierogi; try the potato-and-cheese ones with kefir, plus borscht and crêpes.

name: Amalfi
blurb: Thin-crust pizza from a very hot wood oven, run by Italian owners; simple and good value for one person.
priceText: About 15 zł for a pizza for one person

name: Mleczarnia
blurb: Big pub in a fin-de-siècle building on a quiet street near the courthouse, with dark, cosy wooden interiors over two levels.

name: Setka
blurb: Kitschy, deliberately Communist-style bar open 24/7 with cheap drinks and decent food; a budget late-night stop.
priceText: 4 zł for a glass of beer or a shot of vodka

name: Wrocław Dwarves trail
blurb: Hunt for the small dwarf statues scattered through the city, a playful walk that goes back to the anti-communist Orange Alternative.

name: Zoo Wrocław
blurb: Poland's oldest zoo, opened in 1865 when the city was Prussian Breslau, and the country's largest by number of animals.
priceText: 55 zł adults, 45 zł reduced, 45 zł students

name: Stary Rynek (Old Market Square)
blurb: Medieval square rebuilt after WWII destruction, lined with cafés and bars; one of the finest in Europe and the heart of the old town.

name: Town Hall (Ratusz)
blurb: Gothic town hall later rebuilt in Renaissance style; the centrepiece of the Rynek, with a small entry fee.

name: Brama Poznania (ICHOT)
blurb: Interactive exhibition on Cathedral Island's history and the founding of Poznań, with an audioguide and a rooftop view.

name: Museum of Musical Instruments
blurb: Some 2,000 instruments from around the world, the only collection of its kind in Poland, plus a large Chopin memorabilia section.

name: Pierogarnia Stary Młyn
blurb: Rustic pierogi house with sweet, sour, meat and vegan fillings, plus bigos and żurek; a proper Polish meal.

name: Dramat
blurb: Cheap, perennially popular Polish eatery on the Rynek, good for a budget meal in the Old Town.

name: Kultowa
blurb: Smoky, brick-walled pub playing 80s and 90s Polish rock hits; a slower, relaxed night out.

name: Cuba Libre
blurb: Latin music bar where the owner often gives a short salsa lesson before the DJ-led Latin parties start.

name: Termy Maltańskie
blurb: One of Poland's largest aquaparks, with a wave pool and many slides; sauna and sports-pool zones are paid separately.
when: Aquapark daily 09:00–23:00; sauna zone Mon–Fri 14:30–23:00, Sat–Sun 11:30–23:00 (official site)

name: Morasko Meteorite Nature Reserve
blurb: Nature reserve on the city edge with seven craters left by a meteorite fall thousands of years ago; a free walk outdoors.

name: Topography of Terror
blurb: Free outdoor and indoor history museum on the former Gestapo and SS headquarters site, documenting Nazi terror.

name: East Side Gallery
blurb: The longest surviving stretch of the Berlin Wall, covered in murals painted in 1991 and restored after years of decay. Free.

name: Pergamon Museum
blurb: Classical antiquity and Islamic art in a grand building, but a major refurbishment is under way, so check which halls are open.

name: DDR Museum
blurb: Hands-on look at everyday life in East Germany; you can touch and examine almost every exhibit.

name: Markthalle Neun
blurb: Market hall for food and produce, a practical place to pick up lunch or a picnic. Closed Sundays.

name: Mustafas Gemüse Kebap
blurb: Locally famous döner stand that draws tourists and Berliners at all hours; expect a 20–40 minute wait for your kebab.
priceText: Chicken döner with vegetable €2.90; vegetable kebap €3.50

name: Clärchens Ballhaus
blurb: Ballroom from 1913 with a hall of mirrors, known for swing, salsa, tango and disco nights; dancing starts at 21:00.
priceText: €5 on weekends; usually free on weeknights
when: Daily from 11:00; dance from 21:00; to about 00:00 weeknights, 04:00 weekends

name: Berghain / Panorama Bar
blurb: Legendary techno club in an old cogeneration plant near Ostbahnhof; the Panorama Bar upstairs runs late until Sunday afternoon.
when: Panorama Bar open late, until Sunday afternoon (per source)

name: Bus 100 and 200 city tour
blurb: Ordinary city buses that pass many landmarks between Zoologischer Garten and Alexanderplatz; a cheap sightseeing ride.
when: Every 5–10 minutes, Zoologischer Garten to Alexanderplatz

name: Rübezahl ice rink (Müggelsee)
blurb: Waterside restaurant and beer garden at Müggelsee with an ice-skating rink in winter; the food is good but on the pricey side.
when: Ice rink in winter; dates not listed

name: Elbphilharmonie plaza
blurb: Glass-fronted concert hall on top of an old warehouse; the public plaza up top is free and gives views over the harbour.

name: St. Michaelis (Michel)
blurb: Baroque church and Hamburg's best-known landmark, rebuilt after the earlier church was destroyed in 1750.

name: Museum für Kunst und Gewerbe (MKG)
blurb: Leading museum of applied arts and design, with European, Middle Eastern and Far Eastern collections spanning the ancient world to today.
priceText: Adult €10, reduced €7, children under 18 free, family €17

name: Museumshafen Oevelgönne
blurb: Historic ships and boats moored along the Elbe at Oevelgönne; free to walk along the quay.

name: St. Pauli Fischmarkt
blurb: The classic Sunday fish-bread snack: locals eat it early on Sunday mornings at this market, roughly 05:00 to 09:30.

name: Lühmanns Teestube
blurb: Friendly local café with light fare, wonderful pies and baked goods; the Cornish tea with fresh scones is the thing to order.

name: Zur Ritze
blurb: Almost-legendary bar down a small alley near the Beatlesplatz; almost always open, and a great place to sit and talk all night.

name: Molotow
blurb: Rock-focused concert venue and club on St. Pauli with a Top Ten Bar; gigs and club nights.

name: Tierpark Hagenbeck
blurb: Hamburg's zoo, built on the Hagenbeck animal collection that began in 1863 and opened as a park in 1907.

name: HADAG Elbe ferries
blurb: Low-cost Elbe boat ride on the public transport network; the classic route is ferry 62 from Landungsbrücken to Finkenwerder.
priceText: If you have already bought a HVV day ticket, the ride is free

name: Kölner Dom (cathedral and South Tower)
blurb: Gothic cathedral beside the station; since July 2026 visitors pay a sightseeing fee, and the South Tower climb costs extra.
priceText: South Tower €8 (reduced €4, family €20); treasury €8; tower + treasury €12 (Wikivoyage). Official site: sightseeing fee for tourists since 1 July 2026, amount not shown

name: Römisch-Germanisches Museum
blurb: Roman-era finds from Cologne in the Belgian House; the Dionysos mosaic and Poblicius tomb are closed for now (official site).

name: NS-Dokumentationszentrum
blurb: Former Gestapo headquarters with its prison cells, now the largest regional memorial to the Nazis' victims in Germany.
when: Tue–Fri 10:00–18:00; Sat, Sun, holidays 11:00–19:00; Mon closed

name: Hohenzollern Bridge (locks)
blurb: Rhine bridge beside the cathedral, covered in padlocks that couples leave as a sign of loyalty; a free walk-by.

name: Brauhaus FRÜH am Dom
blurb: Traditional Cologne restaurant at the cathedral, serving Cologne cooking and Kölsch in a proper brewhouse setting.

name: Falafel Habibi
blurb: Small, authentic Lebanese place with traditional dishes and friendly staff; two branches serve the same menu.

name: Sixpack
blurb: Belgian Quarter club that mixes electro and indie with a huge bottled-beer list; expect waits and possible rejection late on.

name: Bootshaus
blurb: One of Germany's top clubs, in a converted harbour warehouse; this is serious clubbing rather than a warm-up bar.

name: KD Rhine river cruise
blurb: Rhine boat trip around Cologne with commentary on the landmarks; cheap, with several departures a day.

name: Neptunbad
blurb: Renovated old bath in Ehrenfeld with a Japanese-style sauna landscape on two levels, plus a full fitness centre.

name: Römerberg
blurb: Frankfurt's historic centre, with the Römer town hall and a 14th–15th-century church; free to stroll.

name: Paulskirche
blurb: Church where Germany's first democratically elected parliament met in 1848 and drafted a constitution that never took effect.

name: Museum für Moderne Kunst (MMK)
blurb: Contemporary art in a boat-shaped building by Hans Hollein, with works by Warhol and Lichtenstein in the permanent collection.

name: Portikus
blurb: Free contemporary-art institution, part of the Städelschule art school; it closes when no exhibition is on.

name: Kleinmarkthalle
blurb: Central indoor market hall with local and international vendors, from fresh produce to ready-to-eat food and drinks.

name: Lahmer Esel
blurb: Traditional Hessian restaurant serving local Ebbelwoi (apple wine) and regional food at fair prices; the garden opens in summer.

name: Club Voltaire
blurb: Cultural tavern open since 1962 with drinks for a mixed crowd; entry is generally free, though some event nights charge a cover.
priceText: Generally free entry; sometimes asks for entry for musicians or lecturers

name: Gibson Club
blurb: Chic club with live and DJ acts, open since 2012; the lines outside look long but move fast.
priceText: €12 (Wikivoyage); official site shows no fixed fee, entry varies by event

name: Eissporthalle ice rinks
blurb: Indoor rink open all year plus outdoor rinks that run only in winter; skate hire and lockers are on site.
when: Outdoor rinks winter only; indoor rink all year (hours not listed)

name: Boulderwelt Frankfurt
blurb: Bouldering hall opened in 2012 with problems for beginners to experts, set by an experienced route-setting crew.

name: Frauenkirche
blurb: Rebuilt after WWII destruction; the golden cross on its dome was donated by Coventry, the English city the Luftwaffe bombed.

name: Zwinger Palace (exhibitions)
blurb: Baroque palace courtyard of fountains and sculptures; the ticket opens the Old Masters gallery with Raphael's Sistine Madonna.
priceText: Combined ticket for the exhibitions: adults €18, reduced €13.50 (official site); palace grounds free

name: Historic Green Vault (Grünes Gewölbe)
blurb: One of Europe's finest goldsmith and decorative-arts collections, in two sections that each need their own timed ticket.
when: Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun 10:00–17:00; Fri 10:00–19:00; closed Tue

name: Fürstenzug (porcelain procession)
blurb: Outdoor porcelain-tile procession of the Saxon rulers on horseback, said to be the world's largest porcelain painting.

name: Cafe Toscana
blurb: Famous café with a pastry shop and restaurant; the cakes are the draw.

name: Hot Shüzzle
blurb: Thai street food cooked by a chef from Thailand; small plates at budget prices in Neustadt.

name: Kraftwerk Mitte
blurb: One of Dresden's largest clubs, in a former coal-fired power plant, with parties, raves and concerts.

name: Hebeda's
blurb: Locals' pub in Neustadt with old East German furniture, cheap beer and a small dance floor, busiest on Friday and Saturday nights.
when: Busiest Fri and Sat nights; hours not listed

name: Ice skating, JoyNext Arena
blurb: Indoor and outdoor ice rinks with skate rental, from late October to early March; Saturday evenings bring a DJ ice disco.
when: Daily late Oct–early Mar; ice disco Saturday evenings

name: Jewish life walk (audio tour, 1933–1945)
blurb: Free English map and audio tracks for a self-guided walk through Jewish life in Dresden from 1933 to 1945; allow several hours.

name: St. Thomas Church (Thomaskirche)
blurb: Church where J. S. Bach worked as cantor from 1723 until his death in 1750; his remains lie under an epitaph near the altar. Free entry.

name: Nikolaikirche
blurb: Starting point of the 1989 peaceful demonstrations against the East German regime; free to enter, donations welcome.

name: Monument to the Battle of the Nations
blurb: 91-metre monument to the 1813 Battle of Leipzig, said to be the biggest monument in Europe.
priceText: Adults €12, reduced €10 (official site); Wikivoyage: students and Leipzig Card holders €10, under 6 free

name: Zum Arabischen Coffe Baum (coffee museum)
blurb: Free museum on coffee culture inside Europe's oldest continuously operating coffee house.

name: Zills Tunnel
blurb: Rustic Saxon restaurant with large portions, a cellar and a courtyard terrace; a classic budget-to-mid meal.

name: Zest
blurb: Vegetarian and vegan restaurant; the strawberry basil smoothie is worth ordering.

name: Moritzbastei
blurb: Old student club bar in a former part of the city wall, with underground cellars and live bands or DJs most nights.
when: Hours not listed; live bands or DJs most nights

name: Flowerpower
blurb: Party bar with a 1970s hippie theme and mostly classic rock; the party often runs past 04:00.

name: Sightseeing tram (Gläserner Leipziger)
blurb: Weekend city tour in a modified tram called the Gläserner Leipziger; the ticket includes a day pass for zone 110.
priceText: €15 per person (includes day ticket for zone 110)

name: Wildpark
blurb: Free wild-animal park in the riverside woods; walk on to Clara-Zetkin Park or Cospudener See for a longer hike.

name: Nuremberg Castle (Imperial Castle)
blurb: Hilltop fortress dominating the old town, made of three distinct parts that once stood in conflict; visit with the combined ticket.
priceText: Combination ticket 10 € regular, 9 € reduced (official site); single sites 7 € and 4 €

name: Memorium Nuremberg Trials
blurb: Courtroom 600 in the Palace of Justice, where the Nazi high command was tried after WWII; an audio guide is included.

name: Germanisches Nationalmuseum
blurb: One of the largest museums of art and crafts in German-speaking countries, from prehistoric finds to 20th-century art; allow half a day.

name: St Sebald Church
blurb: Romanesque church from the 13th century with later Gothic and Baroque additions, on the north side of the old town; free to enter.

name: Historische Bratwurstküche (Zum Guldenen Stern)
blurb: Timber-framed sausage restaurant that claims to be the world's oldest, since 1419; order six or ten grilled sausages.

name: Red Curry House
blurb: Small South-East Asian dishes at low prices, good value for money; closed on Sundays and public holidays.
when: Mon–Sat 11:30–20:30; closed Sun and public holidays

name: Mata Hari Bar
blurb: Small, packed bar where it's easy to strike up conversation, especially if you're on your own; good for long evenings.

name: Die Rakete
blurb: Small electronic-music club that is a regional institution, known well beyond Nuremberg.

name: Nurembergs Underworld (Felsengänge)
blurb: Guided tours through sandstone cellars under the castle hill, including old beer cellars and WWII air-raid shelters.
when: Tours hourly or two-hourly daily; English tours Sat and Sun at 11:15

name: Langwasserbad
blurb: Large indoor pool with a sauna and wellness areas, open daily; towels, slippers and drinks are not included and swimwear is required.

name: Frauenkirche
blurb: Twin-towered cathedral that defines Munich's skyline; the church is free to enter, and the tower climb costs extra.

name: Deutsches Museum
blurb: Enormous science and technology museum that needs a full day; pick your galleries in advance.

name: Schloss Nymphenburg
blurb: Baroque palace that grew from a 17th-century pavilion into a vast residence; around 20 ornate rooms are on view.
priceText: Winter (mid-Oct–Mar): palace 10 € regular, 9 € reduced; combined ticket 16 € / 14 € (official site)

name: Palaeontological Museum
blurb: Free fossil museum with Archaeopteryx, Triceratops and a sabre-toothed cat, in an interesting three-floor building.

name: Viktualienmarkt
blurb: Large open-air food market just south of Marienplatz; a good place for picnic supplies and snacks.

name: Bratwurst Glöckl
blurb: Bavarian restaurant opposite the Frauenkirche, known for small Nürnberger sausages served in sixes.

name: Augustiner Stammhaus
blurb: Original beer hall of the Augustiner brewery, founded in 1294; great atmosphere, beer and traditional Bavarian food.

name: Blitz Club
blurb: Major techno club in the former congress hall of the Deutsches Museum, with a regular international DJ line-up.

name: Müllers'sches Volksbad
blurb: Art Nouveau public swimming baths from 1901; cheap to swim, but bring your own towel. The sauna is temporarily shut.

name: Boulderwelt München Ost
blurb: Large bouldering hall with 13 courses and no harness needed; weekday tickets before 16:00 are cheaper.
